text: The cause is that SQLite returns `expires_at` as a naive datetime, while the code compares it to the timezone-aware `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`. I'm patching `reset_password` to treat a naive stored value as UTC before comparing.

input.diff:
--- a/app/routers/auth.py
+++ b/app/routers/auth.py
@@ -159,3 +159,6 @@
     entry = db.query(PasswordResetToken).filter(PasswordResetToken.token == payload.token).first()
-    if not entry or entry.used or entry.expires_at < datetime.now(timezone.utc):
+    expires_at = entry.expires_at if entry else None
+    if expires_at is not None and expires_at.tzinfo is None:
+        expires_at = expires_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    if not entry or entry.used or expires_at < datetime.now(timezone.utc):
         raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST, detail="Invalid or expired reset token")

text:
The password reset test now passes, and so does the full tests/ directory (30 tests passed).

Cause: SQLite returns PasswordResetToken.expires_at as a naive datetime. reset_password compared it to the timezone-aware datetime.now(timezone.utc), which raised TypeError.

Fix (app/routers/auth.py, reset_password only): if the stored expires_at has no timezone, it is treated as UTC before the comparison. Valid tokens are accepted and expired ones still get a 400. When the token isn't found, the `not entry` check short-circuits before the comparison, so nothing is compared against None.

No tests or other files were changed.
